newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel skips G7 summit to deal with budget.
newsitem.headline: Waigel skips G7 summit to deal with budget.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel will skip the June 20-22 summit of the Group of Seven (G7) rich industrial nations in order to continue budget talks at home, the Bonn finance ministry said on Monday.

Waigel considered it important to make progress in setting the stage for domestic jobs promotion and growth by securing the 1997 and 1998 budget, rather than attend the international summit, the ministry added.
Chancellor Helmut Kohl, Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel and Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt will attend the G7 summit in Denver, Colorado.

The German government aims to nail down the main points of the 1998 budget and adjustments to the 1997 budget by June 25, the date of the next meeting of the financial planning council made up of experts from federal, state and local governments and central bank officials.
